chunks: I heard that in mursal form from the shaykhs and through scholarly discussion, and its chain of transmission is not presently with me; its gist is what he mentioned:

That when Allah, Exalted is He, sent Adam عليه السلام down from the Garden of Abode to the earth, he became lonely, so he asked Allah, Exalted is He, to comfort him with something from the trees of Paradise. Then Allah, Exalted is He, sent down to him the palm tree, and he used to find comfort in it during his life.

Then when death came to him, he said to his children: I used to find comfort in it during my life, and I hope for comfort by it after my death. So when I die, take from it a fresh branch, split it into two halves, and place them with me in my shrouds. His children did that, and the Prophets did it after him.
Then that practice disappeared in the Age of Ignorance, so the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله revived it and performed it, and thus it became an observed sunnah (prophetic tradition).

key_terms.آدَمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Adam, the first Prophet, peace be upon him
key_terms.النَّخْلَةَ: the palm tree sent down as a source of comfort
key_terms.الْأَنْبِيَاءُ: the Prophets who continued this practice
key_terms.الْوَفَاةُ: death, the moment of passing from worldly life
key_terms.جَنَّةِ الْمَأْوَى: the Garden of Abode from which Adam عليه السلام was sent down
key_terms.سُنَّةً مُتَّبَعَةً: an established and followed sunnah (prophetic tradition)

ai.seo_question: What is the origin of placing fresh palm branches with the deceased in Islamic burial practice?
ai.summary: This report recounts that Adam عليه السلام found comfort in a palm tree sent down from Paradise, and at his death instructed that fresh palm branches be placed in his shrouds. The practice was continued by the Prophets, later lost in the Age of Ignorance, and then revived by the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, becoming an established sunnah (prophetic tradition).
